comparison: Perfect agreement on ADC characterization (C33-C37). Both accept the DAR values, binding assays, and in vitro cytotoxicity data as adequate evidence for successful ADC generation and validation. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Perfect agreement on compartment-specific findings (C48-C50). Both acknowledge increased B cells in lymph nodes and spleen preservation. OpenEval notes findings are unexpected but supported; peer reviewers explicitly accept these tissue-specific differences as established facts.

Both address Treg depletion (C38-C40, C51-C53). OpenEval finds flow cytometry data fully supportive with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers acknowledge partial Treg decrease (~40%) as a core finding without challenge. Strong agreement on Treg depletion evidence.

Both evaluate Belatacept experiments (C84-C93, C116). OpenEval describes the experiment as 'elegant' and fully supportive of CD28 costimulation requirement. Peer reviewers find it 'more convincing' and accept T cell activation requirement, though note partial rescue. Agreement on mechanism but peer review emphasizes incompleteness.

Both address TNF-α experiments (C94-C98, C117-C118). OpenEval finds partial rescue supportive of TNF-α as one mediator. Peer reviewers accept the finding but emphasize incomplete reversal suggests additional factors. Agreement on partial role of TNF-α.

Both evaluate T cell depletion experiments (C75-C83, C105, C115, C121). OpenEval finds strong evidence for T cell-mediated B cell destruction. Peer reviewers acknowledge T cell requirement but express major concerns: alternative mechanisms possible (recirculation, T cell death effects), direct killing never demonstrated, only inferred. Significant disagreement on interpretation strength.

Both address T cell activation phenotype (C68-C74). OpenEval finds expansion of effector memory T cells and hyper-proliferative state fully supported. Peer reviewers accept T cell activation and hyperactivation findings without contest. Strong agreement.

Major disagreement on B cell loss interpretation (C43-C44, C55-C58, C61-C62, C64-C65). OpenEval finds selective mature B cell loss with apoptosis well-supported by flow cytometry. Peer reviewers express major concerns: blood B cell drop may reflect recirculation to lymphoid organs rather than depletion; interpretation 'too simplistic'; central premise 'underexplored.' Fundamental disagreement on whether true depletion occurs.

Strong disagreement on apoptosis data (C59-C60). OpenEval finds apoptosis data in peripheral blood supportive and consistent with bone marrow loss. Peer Reviewer 1 directly challenges reliability, noting 80% apoptosis in lymph nodes and 50% in spleen of control mice is 'way too high' and suggests artefactual stress during in vitro processing. Evidence deemed unreliable by peer review.

Both address immunoglobulin increases (C63-C67). OpenEval finds IgE increase consistent with Treg impairment and well-supported. Peer reviewers acknowledge increased plasma immunoglobulins, especially IgE, and increased serum antibody levels without challenge. Agreement on this finding.

Both address payload control specificity (C45-C46, C71). OpenEval finds hIgGFc-DM1 control demonstrates no effect on Tregs, confirming specificity. Peer reviewers accept this control without challenge as supporting specificity. Agreement on control validity.

Both address CTLA-4 expression specificity (C47). OpenEval confirms CTLA-4 expression only in Tregs, not B cells, establishing indirect mechanism. Peer reviewers accept this, with Reviewer 2 noting B cells don't express CTLA-4 so indirect mechanism assumed. Agreement on this finding.

Both address FasL experiments (C98). OpenEval notes anti-FasL has no effect, ruling out this pathway. Peer reviewers accept this negative result without challenge. Agreement that FasL is not a major mediator.
OpenEval evaluates extensive background knowledge claims (C1-C32) as supported by appropriate literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these background claims found.

OpenEval evaluates discussion points (C99-C105) about model recapitulating clinical phenotypes and consistency with literature as supported. Peer review addresses some overlapping mechanistic claims (C105) within R6 but no dedicated evaluation of these discussion claims.

OpenEval evaluates discussion points (C106-C116) comparing to prior literature, including distinction that only mature B cells affected and mechanistic insights. Peer review addresses some overlapping claims (C115, C116) within R6 and R7 but no dedicated evaluation of these comparative discussion points.

OpenEval evaluates discussion points (C119-C122) about CD4/CD8 involvement and T-B cell antagonism as supported. Peer review addresses CD4/CD8 involvement (C121) within R6 but no dedicated evaluation of the T-B antagonism concept.
OpenEval evaluates methods description (C123) for mouse model as appropriately cited. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
